articles.title: Stephen Curry opens up on his vision behind his $400 million move as he looks beyond basketball ahead of the new season
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors' star player, might be one the greatest athletes that the world has ever seen but he has also been a smart bu.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors' star player, might be one the greatest athletes that the world has ever seen but he has also been a smart businessman. Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have set up multiple ventures together and regularly partner with luxury brands. Amid this, the NBA legend has reflected on his $400 million deal.Stephen Curry shares what motivated him to sign a $400 million deal with Li-NingA few days ago, in an interview with NBC Sports Bay Area, the star player Stephen Curry opened up about signing a $400 million deal with Chinese sneaker company, Li-Ning, as he said, “A new energy…”The Golden State Warriors’ star player added, “They’re an incredible innovation engine and machine that I want to tap into to express my love for the game at all levels. Whether you’re an aspiring amateur professional like me, or you’re just getting into the game, there’s a space out here for everybody. I’m excited about that journey.”Stephen Curry also continued, “That’s something that was really important for this partnership, to think about the future – not just while I’m still playing basketball…”The four time NBA champion added, “Ayesha’s getting into the game a little bit, my kids are getting into the game, so you want to have an expression for everybody to enjoy themselves out here and enjoy the fun in golf.”For the unversed, back in November 2025, Stephen Curry sparked shockwaves when he ended his decade long contract with Under Armor.After a few months, the four time NBA champion Stehen Curry announced his partnership with the Chinese sneaker company, Li-Ning, sparking a heated debate.While some criticised his decision and trolled him, others felt it was a smart business move by Stephen Curry.However, the NBA legend has kept himself away from all the speculations as he has kept his focus on the court.Stephen Curry reflects what the upcoming season has in store for the Golden State Warriors as star players remain injuredAhead of the new season, in an interview with The Athletic, Stephen Curry reflected on the upcoming season as he weighed in on Moses Moody and Jimmy Butler’s return from their long-term injuries as he said, “You hope that they both come back healthy. And we can play at a level that keeps us relevant and competitive and builds a foundation so that we can figure out what it looks like.”He added, “But that is the situation. We don’t live in any alternative universe.” “Sure. I’m hopeful for all the creative ideas of getting the best team possible. We had those conversations. But when you have injuries at the top like that, it’s always gonna change.”Stephen Curry has also spent some time in recovery as he gears up for the new season.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Top 7 players to watch in 2026-27 NBA season who are making the biggest injury returns: Luka Doncic, Kyrie Irving and more
articles.summary: NBA News: Several of the league's most recognizable names enter the 2026-27 season working their way back from serious injuries, and how fast they regain form c.
articles.body: Several of the league's most recognizable names enter the 2026-27 season working their way back from serious injuries, and how fast they regain form could reshape the race in both conferences. Luka Doncic, Joel Embiid, Kyrie Irving, Damian Lillard, Tyrese Haliburton, Fred VanVleet and Trae Young headline a group of returning stars whose health will weigh heavily on their teams' postseason outlooks.7 must-watch NBA stars making a comeback in 2026-27These seven players carry outsized influence on their teams' ceilings, and each is dealing with a different stage of recovery heading into training camp. Some, like Young and Doncic, are already cleared and simply need reps. Others, like Irving and Haliburton, are working against a much longer layoff and a coaching staff that may choose caution over urgency in October and November.Luka DoncicTeamLos Angeles Lakers2025-26 stats33.5 PPG, 7.7 RPG, 8.3 APG, 47.6 FG%InjuryGrade 2 left hamstring strainStatusCleared for full basketball activitiesDoncic was cleared for full activity in late May, roughly two and a half weeks after the Lakers were eliminated in the second round by Oklahoma City. The hamstring strain cost him the entire postseason and, with it, a chance to build on the momentum L.A. had generated through March. He spent the offseason resting deliberately, skipping FIBA World Cup qualifiers with Slovenia to be with his daughters, and later hosted teammates for a player-run minicamp in August. Doncic is coming off a scoring title and will look to turn that into deeper playoff success, having been part of just one postseason win since arriving in Los Angeles a season and a half ago.Joel EmbiidTeamPhiladelphia 76ers2025-26 stats26.9 PPG, 7.7 RPG, 3.9 APG, 48.9 FG%InjuryLeft knee, plus an oblique issueStatusOptimistic entering campEmbiid's durability has been the league's longest-running question mark, yet he has still produced MVP-caliber stretches around the absences. He played just 57 of a possible 164 games across the last two seasons, but says the knee itself is no longer the primary concern. An oblique injury and other setbacks limited him more than the knee did. He now has Jaylen Brown and LeBron James around him in Philadelphia, and a healthy Embiid could finally push the 76ers past the conference finals barrier that has eluded every MVP season of his career.Kyrie IrvingTeamDallas Mavericks2024-25 stats24.7 PPG, 4.8 RPG, 4.6 APG, 47.3 FG%InjuryTorn right ACLStatusRamping up via summer pickup gamesDallas shut Irving down at last season's All-Star break once the team's lottery odds became the priority, and he'll be about 19 months removed from surgery when camp opens. He has spent the summer ramping up in pickup games, generating enough highlights to fuel hope that he can pair immediately with Cooper Flagg. League sources told ESPN that other teams are watching closely to see how, or if, the 34-year-old fits Dallas's long-term plans, since a healthy Irving, who has averaged 25.5 points and 5.1 assists per game as a Maverick, could become a trade target if new team president Masai Ujiri is open to moving him before the deadline.Damian LillardTeamPortland Trail Blazers2024-25 stats24.9 PPG, 4.7 RPG, 7.1 APG, 44.8 FG%InjuryTorn AchillesStatusReturning to Portland after three years awayLillard's return doubles as a homecoming, his first time back in Portland since he was traded three years ago. At 36 and coming off an Achilles tear, the questions are less about sentiment and more about fit: how much he has left physically, and how he slots into a Blazers team that made the playoffs last season on the strength of a defense-first identity built around Deni Avdija. Portland now has to integrate both Lillard and newly acquired guard Ja Morant into the backcourt, a project that will shape whether last year's playoff breakthrough was a floor or a ceiling for this roster.Tyrese HaliburtonTeamIndiana Pacers2024-25 stats18.6 PPG, 3.5 RPG, 9.2 APG, 47.3 FG%InjuryAchilles tearStatusChomping at the bit to return, per reportsIt has been 15 months since Haliburton last played, a stretch that ended when he exited Game 7 of the 2025 Finals with the injury. The Eastern Conference has shifted meaningfully since then. Haliburton led Indiana to back-to-back conference finals appearances and came within one game of a title, so the question now is whether his return alone reinserts the Pacers into that tier, or whether Indiana manages his workload early in hopes of peaking again by the postseason.Fred VanVleetTeamHouston Rockets2024-25 stats14.1 PPG, 3.7 RPG, 5.6 APG, 37.8 FG%InjuryTorn right ACL and a torn meniscusStatusFull-time, ramping upVanVleet told Andscape in July he was back on the court "full-time, ramping up, feeling good," and expects to be ready when Houston opens the preseason in Macao. His return restores offensive stability for a Rockets team that struggled to close out games last season once opponents keyed in on Kevin Durant. One byproduct of his absence was extra development time for young guards Amen Thompson and Reed Sheppard, experience the team hopes carries into this season. Assuming no setbacks, VanVleet projects as the primary setup man for Durant and Alperen Sengun.Trae YoungTeamWashington Wizards2025-26 stats17.9 PPG, 2.0 RPG, 8.0 APG, 45.8 FG%InjuryMCL and quadriceps injuries, right legStatusCleared for training campYoung played just five games after Atlanta traded him to Washington in January, and the Wizards were still in rebuilding mode when he arrived. He says the wait has only sharpened his motivation to play alongside Anthony Davis and top pick AJ Dybantsa. "I'm very motivated to be back in the conversation where I should be," Young told ESPN, pushing back on the idea that his value is tied only to scoring or assist totals. He turns 28 later this month and is fully cleared, giving Washington a healthy starting point as it tries to climb out of three straight 60-loss seasons.More NBA players expected to make a comeback soonSeveral other notable names are working back from injury without cracking the top tier of urgency, either because their timelines remain uncertain or their teams are further from contention. Jimmy Butler III, entering his 16th season and the final year of his contract with Golden State, is still rehabbing a right ACL tear; strength tests have shown progress, but a return before January or February looks unlikely given the Warriors' cautious medical approach under Rick Celebrini.Anthony Davis, cleared from a hand injury after playing only 20 games last season split between two teams, looks ready for camp and will pair with Young in Washington's backcourt.In Houston, Steven Adams is targeting a healthy start after ankle surgery limited him to 32 games, a return that matters given the Rockets' reliance on his offensive rebounding and interior defense behind Alperen Sengun.New Orleans point guard DeJounte Murray, who came back from a ruptured Achilles late last season and averaged 16.7 points and 6.4 assists in 14 games, is expected to be full go under new coach Jamahl Mosley.Walker Kessler joins the Lakers fully healed from shoulder surgery, telling reporters in Las Vegas, "sitting out a whole year definitely puts a lot of things in perspective," as he takes on a larger role next to Doncic.Jaren Jackson Jr. is set to anchor Utah's frontcourt after knee surgery limited him to three games following a midseason trade, and Jalen Williams returns to Oklahoma City hoping to shake recurring hamstring strains that undercut last season.Ja Morant begins a fresh chapter in Portland after an elbow injury ended his final Memphis season early, while Memphis center Zach Edey and Sacramento's Domantas Sabonis are both targeting healthy starts following ankle and meniscus procedures, respectively.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors Reveal Pistons' Last Contract Offer amid Qualifying Offer, Kings Buzz
articles.summary: All-Star center Jalen Duren is the only notable NBA restricted free agent who has yet to resolve his contract situation, as he reportedly still hasn't found common ground with the Detroit Pistons.
articles.body:
All-Star center Jalen Duren is the only notable NBA restricted free agent who has yet to resolve his contract situation, as he reportedly still hasn't found common ground with the Detroit Pistons.

According to Sam Amick and Hunter Patterson of The Athletic, Duren is seeking a contract worth at least $200 million, but the Pistons' last offer was for five years and $190 million.

There is reportedly mutual interest between Duren and the Sacramento Kings, but the Pistons have refused to engage with the Kings in sign-and-trade talks.

While a sign-and-trade is the only way for the Kings to potentially land Duren right now, Amick and Patterson noted that Sacramento could have the ability to make room to sign Duren to a max contract next offseason should he become available.

Selected 13th overall in the 2022 NBA draft, Duren has shown marked improvement over the course of his four-year NBA career.

Although he averaged a double-double in both 2023-24 and 2024-25, Duren took his game to the next level last season.

The 6'10" big man averaged a career-high 19.5 points per game on 65.0 percent shooting to go along with 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists.

With Duren as the Pistons' No. 2 offensive option behind Cade Cunningham, the team led the Eastern Conference with a 60-22 record and fell one win short of reaching the Eastern Conference Finals.

As good as Duren was in earning All-Star and All-NBA Third Team honors for the first time, his playoff struggles may have plenty to do with the Pistons' apparent hesitancy to sign him to a huge contract.

Over 14 playoff appearances, Duren's numbers dipped significantly compared to the regular season, as he averaged 10.2 points on 51.4 percent shooting, as well as 8.5 rebounds and 2.1 assists.

While Duren is eligible for a contract extension that would pay him $287 million over five years, the Pistons reportedly haven't come anywhere close to that number.

The Kings seemingly view Duren as a max-level player more than the Pistons do, and Sacramento is reportedly Duren's preferred destination should he go elsewhere due partly to the notion that he could "thrive" alongside rookie first-round pick Darius Acuff Jr.

Per Amick and Patterson, Duren did not attend a team minicamp in San Diego set up by Cunningham last month, nor was he in attendance for team governor Tom Gores' Labor Day party.

That seems to underscore the uncertainty of whether Duren will play for the Pistons this season or beyond.

If the two sides can't agree to a long-term deal before the Pistons' regular-season opener on Oct. 20, a short-term deal with player or team options is a possibility, and that could potentially lead to him becoming an unrestricted free agent next offseason, much like what happened with Jonathan Kuminga from last offseason to this offseason.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Slams Patrick Beverley's Criticism of His NBA Comeback, 'I Worked My Ass Off'
articles.summary: Ben Simmons pushed back on criticism from longtime NBA veteran Patrick Beverley about his comeback after signing with the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons pushed back on criticism from longtime NBA veteran Patrick Beverley about his comeback after signing with the Sacramento Kings.

In response to an Instagram video in which Beverley cited players like Victor Oladipo, Gabe Vincent and Cam Thomas as still looking for an NBA team while Simmons got signed after a year out of the league, the two-time All-Star commented with a stern defense of his work to make it back on a roster:

"Walk away….?? 😂😂😂I played two years not physically right. This ain't no hand out. I worked my ass off to be in this position…. And I'm very grateful to even be in position to play the game I f---king love! Yall will continue to make up stories for your own benefits and that's more telling about who yall are."

Ranking the NBA's Top 10 Trade Targets 🎯

Simmons is joining the Kings on a one-year deal after sitting out the 2025-26 season. His last appearance in an NBA game was on April 29, 2025, for the Los Angeles Clippers in a playoff game against the Denver Nuggets.

The addition of Simmons provides the Kings with more point guard depth. Darius Acuff Jr., the No. 7 pick in the 2026 draft, is penciled in as the starter. He figures to endure some growing pains adjusting to the NBA.

Even though Simmons is no longer one of the best all-around point guards, he still has the court vision to get an offense organized, especially in transition.

Simmons also has the size to play other positions, which will provide head coach Doug Christie with some versatility as he tries to piece things together for the 2026-27 season.

There's no risk on the Kings' part since Simmons is making the veteran minimum. If he ends up being a useful player for them, they will get more than their money's worth. If not, it won't really cost them anything to move on.

articles.title: Kevin Durant Eyeing 5th Team USA Gold Medal at 2028 LA Olympics, 'It's an Incredible Time'
articles.summary: Although he will be nearly 40 years old when the 2028 Summer Olympics take place in Los Angeles in two years, Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has his sights set on playing for the United States men's basketball team once again.
articles.body:
Although he will be nearly 40 years old when the 2028 Summer Olympics take place in Los Angeles in two years, Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has his sights set on playing for the United States men's basketball team once again.

According to Nick Friedell of The Athletic, Durant made it clear at a recent USA Basketball charity event that LA28 is firmly on his radar.

That backed up comments Durant made about the Olympics late in the 2025-26 season when he told reporters, "It's just fun, man. It's an incredible time. You get to travel the world. I don't know if we're gonna get to travel the world with it being in the States, but the last few years, we would go [to] Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Paris, London, Canary Islands, Madrid … being in places that changed not just my perspective about the game, just about life in general. I've been in places I've never even thought about being in if it wasn't for the game. That experience is one of the best, man. I encourage everybody to play for their country."

Ranking the NBA's Top 10 Trade Targets 🎯

Durant has played for Team USA at each of the past four Summer Olympics, and he played a big role in the Americans winning the gold medal on all four occasions.

KD's four Olympic gold medals are already the most ever by a men's basketball player, and he can extend that record by winning a fifth at what would be his fifth Olympic Games.

A strong argument can already be made for Durant being the greatest Team USA basketball player of all time, as he is the United States' all-time leading scorer at the Olympics with 518 points to go along with his four gold medals.

Durant was the second-oldest player on the last Olympic team in Paris in 2024, but with LeBron James announcing that the 2024 Olympics would be his last, KD will almost certainly be the elder statesman in 2028 if he makes the squad.

While nothing is guaranteed for a player of Durant's age, the 16-time NBA All-Star continues to play at an elite level.

Last season, the 37-year-old veteran averaged 26.0 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 2.4 three-pointers made per game. He was also highly efficient, shooting 52.0 percent from the field and 41.3 percent from beyond the arc.

Perhaps most impressively, Durant played in 78 of the Rockets' 82 regular-season games, marking his most games played since the 2018-19 season.

If KD can stay healthy over the next two years, there is no reason to think he doesn't have the ability to make a fifth Olympic team, especially since he continues to be one of the most lethal scorers in the NBA nearly two decades into his career.

articles.title: Jalen Duren Has The Pistons In A $200 Million Pickle
articles.summary: Jalen Duren has turned a breakout season into a contract standoff with the Detroit Pistons. The young center now has to decide whether locking in a huge deal...
articles.body:
Jalen Duren has turned a breakout season into a contract standoff with the Detroit Pistons . The young center now has to decide whether locking in a huge deal is worth giving up the chance to bet on himself.

Duren made his first All-Star team and earned All-NBA Third Team honors last season. Those honors gave him the leverage to push for a contract that reaches well beyond $200 million.

Jalen Duren And Detroit Are Still Stuck On The Money

According to The Athletic's latest reporting , Detroit has raised its offer to five years and $190 million, while Duren's camp wants at least $200 million. That creates a $10 million gap in total value, or about $2 million per season over five years.

The money is only part of the fight. Duren's camp can point to a 2025-26 season in which he averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds while helping Detroit win 60 games. He also became a first-time All-Star and earned his first All-NBA selection.

The Pistons have a different memory of the season. Duren's production fell sharply in the playoffs, when he averaged 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds across 14 games. He also finished the postseason with a negative plus-minus, giving Detroit a reason to hesitate before making a massive commitment.

That creates the central problem for Detroit. The front office is being asked to pay for the player who dominated the regular season, while its biggest concern comes from the version that appeared when the pressure increased.

Jalen Duren Could Bet On Himself For One More Year

Duren has another option that would change the entire negotiation. He can accept his $9.6 million qualifying offer for 2026-27, play the season and become an unrestricted free agent next summer.

That would give Duren a chance to rebuild his market value. It would also put a huge amount of guaranteed money at risk if he suffers an injury or fails to match last season's production.

The situation is more complicated because Duren is eligible for a five-year deal worth up to $287.1 million after making the All-NBA team. Other teams cannot match Detroit's ability to offer five years, which gives the Pistons leverage even while negotiations remain stuck.

The Pistons also have another reason to stay patient. They are building around Cade Cunningham and need to decide how much of their future payroll should go toward their frontcourt.

For Duren, the choice is just as serious. He can secure generational money now, or risk millions by betting that another strong season will make him even more valuable.

Detroit and Duren are not arguing over whether he is valuable. They are arguing over how much that value is worth.

And with $200 million sitting in the middle of the dispute, neither side has blinked yet.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Claps Back At Patrick Beverley After Landing Kings Deal
articles.summary: Ben Simmons is getting another chance to prove he can still help an NBA team. The Sacramento Kings gave him a one-year deal after watching him work out and g...
articles.body:
Ben Simmons is getting another chance to prove he can still help an NBA team. The Sacramento Kings gave him a one-year deal after watching him work out and go through medical testing, creating a low-commitment chance for the former All-Star to restart his career.

The timing also fits Sacramento's roster needs. The Kings drafted Darius Acuff Jr. seventh overall this summer, so adding an experienced passer gives coach Doug Christie another option while the rookie adjusts to the NBA game.

Ben Simmons Has A Chance To Bring Back His Best Traits

Sacramento is not asking Ben Simmons to become the player who once made three All-Star teams. His value now is more specific, with his passing and size giving the Kings another way to move the ball and defend across the lineup.

Simmons last played 51 games during the 2024-25 season with Brooklyn and the Clippers. He averaged 5.0 points, 5.6 assists and 4.7 rebounds before spending all of the following season outside the NBA.

The Kings still went through a full evaluation before signing him. Simmons completed medical exams, an on-court workout and meetings with Christie and team staff before the agreement became official.

That process matters because Sacramento did not simply hand Simmons a roster spot based on his old reputation. The team had a chance to see where he is physically and what he can offer now.

Patrick Beverley Questioned Why Simmons Got Another Shot

That opportunity drew the attention of Patrick Beverley , who questioned why Simmons had another NBA job while players such as Victor Oladipo , Gabe Vincent and Cam Thomas remained outside the league.

Simmons took the criticism personally and answered Beverley on Instagram .

I played two years not physically right. This ain't no hand out. I worked my ass off to be in this position…. And I'm very grateful to even be in position to play the game I f—king love!"

Simmons also pushed back at the idea that outside observers understand what went into his absence. "Yall will continue to make up stories for your own benefits," he wrote.

That response puts the focus back on the part of Simmons' comeback that fans cannot easily see. He says the last two years were not about choosing to leave basketball behind, but about trying to get his body right and earn another opportunity. The Kings have now given him one.

Ben Simmons Has Less To Prove Than He Used To

Ben Simmons was once expected to become one of the league's best two-way guards after Philadelphia selected him No. 1 overall in 2016. He won Rookie of the Year, made three All-Star teams and earned All-NBA honors before injuries changed the direction of his career.

Sacramento does not need that entire version to return. It needs a healthy veteran who can organize an offense, defend multiple positions and help a young roster survive difficult stretches.

That makes the one-year contract a useful test for both sides. Simmons gets another NBA stage, while the Kings get a close look at a player with skills they believe can still translate.

Beverley questioned why Simmons was the one who got that chance. Simmons has answered him in the only way that ultimately settles the argument.

Now he has to make the opportunity count.

articles.title: Clippers Reach A Breaking Point As Steve Ballmer Stands Firm
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers are trying to move forward with a major part of their organization suspended. The franchise still has basketball business to finish,...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers are trying to move forward with a major part of their organization suspended. The franchise still has basketball business to finish, but its usual chain of command has been thrown off by the NBA's punishment of several top executives.

That disruption is already affecting one of the team's biggest pending moves. The trade sending Kawhi Leonard to Toronto has not been finalized, even after the NBA completed its investigation and handed down its penalties.

Clippers Are Trying To Navigate A New Power Structure

Steve Ballmer has been suspended for one year, while president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank is suspended for six months. President of business operations Gillian Zucker also received a one-year suspension, leaving the Clippers to reorganize their leadership at a critical point in the offseason.

That has created an unusual problem for the franchise. "No one is running the Clippers right now," Pablo Torre said while discussing the situation .

The Clippers still expect the Leonard trade with Toronto to go through, according to multiple reports. The delay now appears to be tied to the front office changes rather than to a disagreement over the basketball deal itself.

Steve Ballmer Has More At Stake Than A League Punishment

The NBA fined the Clippers $30 million and stripped the team of five future first-round picks after finding multiple salary-cap violations connected to Leonard's off-court income opportunities. Ballmer was suspended after the league said he knowingly helped Leonard obtain outside income.

Torre believes Ballmer's refusal to concede anything during settlement discussions has a wider legal context. "The primary explanation for why Steve Ballmer would not want to concede anything," Torre said, is tied to "every other thing happening to him in the real world."

Those issues include legal and regulatory scrutiny involving Aspiration, the now-defunct company linked to Leonard's endorsement deal. Torre pointed to a civil lawsuit involving Aspiration investors and ongoing SEC investigations.

"There is a civil suit brought by 11 Aspiration investors," Torre said.

The Justice Department is now conducting a criminal investigation into the Clippers' dealings with Leonard, according to Reuters . The investigation includes at least one subpoena and follows the NBA's finding that the team violated its salary-cap rules.

That changes the stakes for Ballmer. Fighting the NBA's ruling is one matter, but admitting wrongdoing could have consequences beyond the league.

The Clippers have continued to deny wrongdoing and called the NBA investigation biased. Meanwhile, the franchise has to rebuild its leadership structure while trying to finish the Leonard trade and prepare for the season.

The basketball side cannot wait forever. But for Ballmer, Torre's argument is that the larger legal fight may explain why he is willing to hold his ground.

articles.title: Suns center Mark Williams reportedly will miss extended period of time after undergoing shoulder surgery
articles.summary: Phoenix re-signed Williams this summer after he appeared in a career-high 60 games for the team during the 2025-26 campaign.
articles.body:
Injuries have held back Mark Williams throughout his NBA career, ostensibly including when a failed physical reportedly nixed a February 2025 trade that would have sent the center to the Los Angeles Lakers .

But Williams appeared in a personal-best 60 games for the Phoenix Suns last season. Following what was the healthiest campaign in his soon-to-be five-year professional career, the Suns re-signed him to a three-year, $38 million deal this summer during free agency.

Unfortunately for the Suns, their odds of getting that much run out of Williams in 2026-27 have reportedly taken a hit. Williams will miss an "extended period of time" after undergoing surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder, ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday .

The injury occurred in an offseason workout, per Charania.

articles.standfirst: Miguel Mendez y Alba Torrens hablan de la semifinal del Mundial femenino de Baloncesto
articles.summary: Miguel Mendez y Alba Torrens hablan de la semifinal del Mundial femenino de Baloncesto
articles.body: Mientras Estados Unidos decidía renunciar a su derecho a entrenar en el Uber Arena y buscaba otra cancha (el Max-Schmeling-Halle), España sí completó su última práctica antes de jugar en esa cancha el partido de semifinales del Mundial ante la vigente campeona. Ante la prensa aparecieron Miguel Méndez y Alba Torrens como seleccionador y capitana para trasladar a todos las sensaciones de un vestuario que vive con mucha ilusión poder jugar unas semifinales después de no haber estado en el último Mundial. Méndez comenzó agradeciendo la presencia de Pau Gasol, que habló al vestuario con la experiencia que da haber ganado el Mundial: "Nos ha hablado de la singularidad de ganar un título como este, que no siempre pasa. Él se ha puesto de ejemplo y nos ha dicho que, con el equipazo que tenían, solo lo ha ganado una vez, nadie sabe si se va a volver a repetir. Así que tenemos que competirlo al máximo, pero también disfrutarlo al máximo". Luego entró en detalle sobre el reto que será jugar ante EEUU: "Son un equipazo y el hecho de que se tomen el partido muy en serio marca el grado de respeto que nos tienen. Han pasado un partido malo, curiosamente el segundo del Mundial, como nosotros, y es raro que puedan repetir otro partido malo. Somos nosotros los que tenemos que provocar que tengan ese partido malo. Tenemos que ser muy valientes e ir a por ellas. Hay que poner nuestro baloncesto sobre la pista". Las derrotas, en este caso, enseñan menos de lo habitual: "No nos vale coger el partido ante Italia como ejemplo porque no es la realidad de cómo juegan, igual que tampoco vale que cojan el nuestro ante Mali. Cuando la mente no está, el cuerpo no responde". Sobre la defensa rival: "Juegan con mucha intensidad y con una gran rapidez de manos, y tenemos que subir al siguiente nivel, pasar de pantalla. Hay que ser muy agresivas porque todas sus jugadoras tienen puntos". La oportunidad de ganar a Estados Unidos está en la mente de todos. Un momento histórico. "Para mí ya lo es porque nunca he vivido unas semifinales del Mundial. Tenemos que intentar aprovechar nuestra oportunidad porque no sabemos quién estará aquí en el próximo Mundial. Esto cambia de un mes para otro. Hay que aprovechar cada oportunidad que tengamos de competir al máximo nivel. Esta generación tiene que aprovecharlo, tiene que disfrutar, pero lo tiene que hacer compitiendo. Tenemos que intentar ganarlas desde el respeto que les tenemos". Méndez habló de la responsabilidad de tenerlo tan cerca: "No debemos caer en el sobreanálisis, tenemos que tratar de sacar los puntos débiles de las norteamericanas, tratar de jugar al ritmo que mejor nos convenga y, de ahí, atacar según nuestras virtudes". La capitana, Alba Torrens, es la única superviviente del equipo que jugó el último Mundial para España en 2018. Valoraba así estar en las semifinales: "Hemos recorrido un largo camino para estar aquí, pero a la vez con la mirada en el presente. Nos hemos estado preparando para el partido del sábado y tenemos que competir por la victoria. Cuando has estado aquí durante un tiempo, le das muchísimo valor. Después de no estar en el pasado Mundial y ahora hablar de unas semifinales te das cuenta del trabajo, no solo del equipo que está aquí, sino de la gente que ha habido alrededor de él y que han remado para estar aquí". Sobre Estados Unidos, el rival del sábado, habla la capitana: "Sabemos que son las favoritas, pero somos conscientes de que en un partido todo puede pasar. En nuestra mano está prepararnos lo mejor posible y mañana vamos a salir a ganar".

Since Caitlin Clark’s rookie season, several WNBA players have used the increased spotlight to exhibit bratty behavior, entitlement, and racial hysteria. By contrast, Cunningham has embraced the moment. She’s entertaining, humorous, resilient, and gorgeous. Colin Cowherd interviewed Cunningham this week on his Volume podcast network, of which she is a part, and noticed a difference between her and the many other athletes he has interviewed. "You are kind of viewed as the leagues…ummm," Cowherd hesitated. "Just say it," Cunningham interrupted. "Sex symbol," he responded. "That is way better, I thought you were gonna go somewhere completely different," she joked. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Contrast Cunningham’s response with Angel Reese’s. Last month, Reese called herself "beautiful" multiple times and bragged that she looks good in a bikini. She then accused internet users of "sexualizing" her in the comments beneath those photos. Many WNBA players want to be seen as sex symbols but then complain about the perception of such. Since a little girl, I've always loved to dress up. I love dresses. I love high heels. I love all of that," Cunningham explained. "For some reason, our society, if you play basketball, you can't dress that way, or you can't be girly. No one's ever said it, but it's like, they kind of feel that you can't be both. Screw all that. Yes, you can. You can be girly, and you can go out and kick someone's ass." She’s right. Of course they do. It’s their only card. In reality, Cunningham is the type of woman Americans would embrace regardless of her skin color. She’s a smoking-hot badass who protects her teammates and trolls the media elite. articles.title: Luwawu-Cabarrot presenta sus credenciales como nueva estrella del Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: El alero francés lidera con 26 puntos el triunfo de los blancos ante La Laguna Tenerife (90-97) en el Torneo Costa del Sol
articles.summary: El alero francés lidera con 26 puntos el triunfo de los blancos ante La Laguna Tenerife (90-97) en el Torneo Costa del Sol
articles.body: Luwawu-Cabarrot irrumpe con fuerza en el ecosistema del Real Madrid. El alero fue la estrella en la victoria blanca en el Sergio Scariolo ante La Laguna Tenerife por 90-97. El de Cannes firmó un partido colosal, echándose el juego ofensivo del equipo de Pedro Martínez a la espalda. El ex de Baskonia fue una amenaza total y acabó el encuentro con 26 puntos y 3 rebotes, para un total de valoración de 27. Shulga sentenció el partido desde el perímetro, pero su partido fue muy discreto hasta el tramo final. A pesar de las muchas caras nuevas, el conjunto merengue sigue dependiendo mucho de Tavares y Campazzo, que acumularon la mayoría de minutos. Los madrileños estuvieron por delante todo el segundo tiempo, aunque no dieron sensaciones de dominar ante la vieja guardia de un Tenerife que, a pesar de estar bajo los mandos de Lakovic, sigue manteniendo el aroma de Txus Vidorreta en muchos sentidos. Comenzó el Real Madrid fuerte en Marbella. Los blancos obraban un parcial de cinco puntos alternando a Tavares y Campazzo que hacía pensar que el partido iba a ser lo de siempre para los madrileños. El encuentro era un constante golpe contra golpe en el juego exterior. El choque avanzaba al ecuador del primer cuarto convertido en un Okeke contra Guy desde la línea de 6,75 para deleite de los aficionados que acudieron a Marbella a ver el partido. Fue el momento entonces de Luwawu-Cabarrot. El ex de Baskonia iba a dar un recital en Marbella e iba a ser el máximo anotador de los blancos, que se fueron por delante con un 25-29 al final de los primeros diez minutos. El segundo acto comenzó con canasta de Gaby Deck. El argentino regresaba a las pistas tras sus problemas en el hombro. Su partido fue intermitente, quizás como algo programado por Pedro Martínez. Los derroteros del encuentro iban por el mismo camino, intercambio de canastas en las dos partes de pista. Van Beck empataba el partido a 34 aprovechando un despiste defensivo de los madrileños. Luwawu-Cabarrot clavaba de nuevo dos triples consecutivos que volvían a despegar a los blancos en el marcador. A pesar de ello, la vieja guardia de Tenerife, con Shermadini, Guy y Abromaitis, daba la vuelta al marcador y ponía a los de Lakovic de nuevo por delante a poco del descanso, al que se llegaría 53-49. El comienzo tras la pausa fue mucho mejor para el Real Madrid. Los de Pedro Martínez probaron un small ball que les funcionó a la perfección para adelantar a su rival. Jantunen mandaba el partido al tiempo muerto con un triple que puso en pie al pabellón Sergio Scariolo. El Madrid se fue con superioridad, pero de nuevo comenzó a pecar en defensa para seguir dejando con vida a los isleños. Con respecto a las caras nuevas en los blancos, Okeke y Luwawu-Cabarrot eran sin duda la nota positiva. El ex de Baskonia cuajó un verdadero partidazo, yéndose por encima de los 20 puntos antes del último cuarto. Pedro Martínez pedía rebotes y ritmo de cara al último tramo de partido con 70-76 para el conjunto madridista. A pesar de los avisos de su entrenador, el rebote siguió siendo un dolor de cabeza para el Real Madrid. Doornekamp era una pesadilla para los madridistas en este aspecto. El último cuarto bajó mucho en ritmo e intensidad, así como en el acierto, todo muy propio de la pretemporada. Cabe recordar que este encuentro era el cuarto para el cuadro tinerfeño y el tercero para el Madrid. El conjunto blanco se llevó el partido finalmente por 90-97 y se citará este sábado en el Martín Carpena con el Unicaja para dilucidar el ganador de la XV edición del Trofeo Costa del Sol.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham Has One Big Request for WNBA Media as League Visibility Grows
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham has become one of the most talked-about figures in women’s basketball. Whether on or off the court, Cunningham’s outspoken personality has...
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has become one of the most talked-about figures in women's basketball. Whether on or off the court, Cunningham's outspoken personality has built a large following for herself and has recently added a new platform to that reach.

The Indiana Fever guard launched a podcast called "No Hesitation" alongside trainer Drew Hanlen . Her debut episode was released on Thursday. During that episode, she addresses the storytelling path she believes the WNBA media should tread. Also, she highlights things she could do differently if she held certain governmental powers over the game.

Sophie Cunningham Wants WNBA Media To Tell More Positive Stories

So far in the season, Cunningham has averaged 8.3 points , 2.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game, demonstrating her central role to her team's success all-year-long. During the show, Cunningham touched on players' remuneration, the WNBA media coverage, and even the outgoing commissioner's office. An NFL-themed X page, Franco Vision, shares snippets from the conversation.

"We're always as players going to want more money, and as owners they're always not going to want to give it to you…"When it comes to media coverage, I think that we have good coverage now. Yes, it can always be better. Yes, it can be bigger." It's all about visibility. And so I do think that we are getting to have that visibility…Now it's on the WNBA media to actually tell the good stories, to tell the positive stories, to actually talk about basketball and how freaking awesome our league is playing this year." It's also in all of us who are part of the WNBA community, to do our part to make it a positive experience for everybody."

"We're always as players going to want more money, and as owners they're always not going to want to give it to you…"When it comes to media coverage, I think that we have good coverage now. Yes, it can always be better. Yes, it can be bigger."

It's all about visibility. And so I do think that we are getting to have that visibility…Now it's on the WNBA media to actually tell the good stories, to tell the positive stories, to actually talk about basketball and how freaking awesome our league is playing this year."

It's also in all of us who are part of the WNBA community, to do our part to make it a positive experience for everybody."

She admitted that the WNBA is a b usiness in which ownership groups have poured substantial investment into franchises. As a result, there's no surprise that periodic tensions between players and the league office inevitably arise. However, beyond arbitrarily eliminating disagreements, Cunningham is more concerned about ensuring that the relationship is built on openness rather than distance.

The WNBA star also addressed a question that has trailed the league all season, surrounding the WNBA's next commissioner. In the bid to answer what she would do differently if she became a commissioner, Cunningham highlighted a few crucial topics that mattered to her. Yet, she still found a way to be lighthearted about her contributions, suggesting that she'd best fit the role of the WNBA's next commissioner.

Cunningham claimed she would prioritize practice facilities, noting that some teams still lack adequate spaces. She highlighted that some athletes are forced to use gyms shared with youth camps, highlighting Fever's own upgrade as proof that transformation is feasible.

Her views come only days after current commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced plans to step down at the end of the 2026 season, closing out a seven-year run marked by rapid growth in attendance, ratings, and media rights value, alongside tension between the league and its players. As the WNBA looks for its next leader, bar the light humor that laced her perspectives and voices, like Cunningham's, suggests players want a seat at that conversation, however little.

articles.title: Warriors Trade Pitch Sends Jimmy Butler to Surprising Team for 3-Time All-Star
articles.summary: A bold Warriors trade pitch sends Jimmy Butler to an unexpected destination while bringing a three-time All-Star to Golden State. The post Warriors Trade Pit...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors cannot afford to waste another season of Stephen Curry 's closing championship window. Curry is entering the final year of his contract, Jimmy Butler is rehabilitating a torn ACL and the Western Conference continues to get younger.

A hypothetical three-team trade for Domantas Sabonis would give Golden State another All-Star without exhausting the assets it may need for a bigger swing later.

Golden State Warriors receive: Domantas Sabonis

Sacramento Kings receive: Patrick Williams , Isaac Okoro , Jalen Smith , Tre Jones , Golden State's 2032 first-round pick, top-10 protected, Chicago 's 2032 first-round pick, protected Nos. 1-20

The proposed picks could convert into second-rounders if they do not convey. This is a trade concept, not a reported negotiation.

Golden State would exchange Butler's $56.8 million expiring contract for Sabonis' $45.5 million salary, reducing its payroll by more than $11 million.

Sacramento would turn one expensive veteran into four younger players and two protected first-round picks. NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that the Kings want positive value for Sabonis, who changed representation and is seeking another extension.

Chicago's incentive would be longer-term financial flexibility.

The Bulls would add approximately $9.6 million in salary this season, but Butler's contract would expire next summer. More importantly, Chicago would escape the final $36 million owed to Williams over the following two seasons.

That would create greater flexibility to construct the roster around Caleb Wilson , Matas Buzelis and Chicago's other young players. Butler could also mentor Wilson, the fourth overall pick in the 2026 NBA draft, while completing his rehabilitation.

Butler would provide a demanding veteran voice with experience playing meaningful postseason basketball. His preparation and ability to read NBA defenses could benefit Wilson, a 19-year-old forward expected to become a centerpiece of Chicago's rebuild.

The Bulls' first must be heavily protected because they should not risk a premium selection merely to clear Williams' contract.

Sabonis would give Curry an elite screener, rebounder and dribble-handoff partner. The three-time All-Star can initiate offense from the elbows and punish smaller defenders around the basket.

His fit becomes more compelling with Kristaps Porziņģis remaining in Golden State.

Porziņģis' perimeter shooting would pull opposing centers away from the paint, opening space for Sabonis. On defense, the 7-foot-2 Porziņģis could provide the rim protection Sabonis lacks. Sabonis would absorb much of the physical rebounding burden that has contributed to Porziņģis' durability concerns.

Draymond Green could move to the bench, organize the second unit and continue closing games when matchups demand his defense.

Sabonis has two guaranteed seasons worth approximately $94 million remaining. Golden State would need assurances about his extension expectations before proceeding.

Warriors Preserve Trey Murphy Ammunition

The trade would leave the Warriors with Porziņģis, Moses Moody , extension-eligible Brandin Podziemski and most of their premium draft capital.

That matters if Trey Murphy III eventually becomes available.

Murphy is not presently on the market, but Golden State and New Orleans held trade discussions before the 2026 draft. Another disappointing Pelicans season could prompt New Orleans to reconsider its direction.

The Warriors could then assemble an offer around Porziņģis, Podziemski and multiple first-round picks. Until then, a Porziņģis-Sabonis frontcourt would give Curry a complementary combination of size, shooting, passing and rebounding without eliminating Golden State's path to another blockbuster.

articles.title: Colin Cowherd believes Sophie Cunningham is the WNBA’s sex symbol
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham was waiting for Colin Cowherd to describe her in a very specific way. Where he ended up going was certainly a choice. Cunningham appeared o...
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham was waiting for Colin Cowherd to describe her in a very specific way. Where he ended up going was certainly a choice.

Cunningham appeared on The Colin Cowherd Podcast to discuss, in part, the rebranding of her podcast from Show Me Something to No Hesitation , which also includes a co-host swap. Cunningham scoffed at the notion that the change was related to her comments about transgender athletes , something former co-host West Wilson publicly disagreed with her about .

In that conversation, Cowherd had a different line of thought for the WNBA player, who has become a lightning rod since those comments and who some have used to turn the women's basketball league into a narrative factory. At one point, he started lining up a question for Cunningham, though it wasn't the one she might have been expecting.

"You are kind of viewed a little bit as the league's…ummm," Cowherd said, looking for the right words.

"Just say it," Cunningham interrupted. "I don't care."

"Sex symbol," he responded. "Is that fair?"

"That is way better," said Cunningham. "I thought you were gonna go somewhere completely different."

"You're tough. You'll fight anybody. You'll taunt anybody. But you'll make sure coming into the arena, 'I look good, and I want you to know I look good.'"

More than a few people wished 62-year-old Colin Cowherd had pumped the brakes a little on this one, especially since Cunningham's podcast is part of his network, which made it even cringier.

All of which is fine, except that the conversation feels strange and out-of-touch when you realize Cowherd could have been describing so many other WNBA players that way .

Strong, tough women's basketball players have worn stylish, striking fashion before games for years , with many of them doubling as models.

A'ja Wilson, Skylar Diggins-Smith, DiJonai Carrington , Angel Reese , Rickea Jackson , and Cameron Brink , just to name a few, have all become well-known for how tough they are on the court and how fashionable they are off it .

Cunningham leaned into Cowherd's assessment, saying, "For some reason, our society, if you play basketball, you can't dress that way, or you can't be girly. No one's ever said it, but it's like, they kind of feel that you can't be both. Screw all that. Yes, you can. You can be girly, and you can go out and kick someone's ass."

Again, that's a good sentiment, but it's not as though WNBA players haven't been pushing back against that stigma for years .

Before Cowherd referred to Cunningham as a sex symbol, she presumed that he was going to call her something else. And one is left to wonder whether that presumption correlates with why the blonde-haired role player is being presented here as the WNBA's superiorly attractive player.

articles.title: Michigan MCBB Unveils 2026 Championship Rings in Video, Photos to Celebrate 1st Title Since 1989
articles.summary: The Michigan men's basketball team is celebrating their 2026 national title run with a trio of rings.
articles.body:
The Michigan men's basketball team is celebrating their 2026 national title run with a trio of rings.

The Wolverines unveiled a first look Friday at rings celebrating the program's Big Ten regular-season championship, Final Four bid and national championship game victory from last season.

Former Michigan stars including the Oklahoma City Thunder's Aday Mara and Golden State Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg posted about opening the ring boxes Friday on social media.

Each national championship ring features the player's name and number alongside a piece of net from Michigan's title game win over UConn.

That side of the ring also features the phrase "37 wins" in honor of the team's program-best 37-3 record last season.

The inside of the ring features coach Dusty May's adapted "April habits" motto as well as the phrase "Shock the world, boys" in honor of the sign Glen Rice held up after the program's title win in 1989.

The Big Ten regular-season championship ring notes on one side the Wolverines went 10-0 on the road and 19-1 in conference play.

The inside of the conference ring highlights the Wolverines' five wins over four top-10 ranked teams in Nebraska, Purdue, Illinois and Michigan State.

The Final Four ring opens to reveal an engraved image of the court in Indianapolis.

Michigan's 69-63 over UConn back on April 6 marked the program's first championship since 1989 as well as the Big Ten's first title since Michigan State won in 2000.

A trio from that team ended up as NBA draft lottery selections in Mara, Lendeborg and Morez Johnson Jr., marking the first time Michigan has sent three players into the first round of the draft since 1990.

articles.body: Bronny James made it through the wildest offseason of his young career without losing his roster spot. His future in the purple and gold has been in question after his father, LeBron James, decided to leave the roster to join the Philadelphia 76ers.The guard now finds himself squeezed for minutes after the Lakers rebuild their roster and LeBron James left the franchise behind. The clock on proving himself is ticking louder than ever heading into 2026-27.Bronny James gets Lakers future warningNothing suggests Bronny James is getting traded or waived any time soon. But the runway is shorter than it looked a year ago, and the Lakers' front office has made that much clear through their offseason moves.Jacob Rude of Silver Screen and Roll captured the mood surrounding Bronny's situation, writing that the Lakers have shown patience with his growth but are starting to expect more from him. In Rude's words, “As much as he has shown signs of progress, though, the time has come for him to be more than a project and to make good on the team’s investment in him.”His contract is fully guaranteed for next season, so there's no financial reason for Los Angeles to move on early. He also made it through the roster shakeup that claimed several other spots. For now, he's expected to report to training camp with the team.Still, the Lakers have to trim their roster before the season tips off, which puts real weight on how Bronny performs in the coming weeks. A starting job isn't realistic. Even a bigger bench role looks tough given how crowded the backcourt has become with new additions.Bronny James understands his role with the LakersBronny isn't pretending the picture is simple. Asked what part of his game needed the most work, he laid out a wide list of goals rather than picking one lane. He needs to be a threat off the ball playing alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, and he knows scoring is part of that."I need to be able to knock down shots and create for others," Bronny recently said, describing where his focus lies this season.Los Angeles is currently carrying 16 players for 15 spots, and most signs point to Jarred Vanderbilt, Dalton Knecht, or Jaden Hardy as the likely cut, not Bronny. The date that would have let the Lakers save money by releasing him has already passed, which suggests they want one more year to watch him grow.The Lakers hold a team option on the final year of his deal, meaning they could move on next summer without any cap consequences. articles.title: “I think the strongest way that you can be is vulnerable and honest”: How LeBron James’ wife Savannah James is challenging the stigma around men’s mental health
articles.summary: NBA News: LeBron James has spent years in the spotlight as one of the biggest names in sports. Away from the NBA court, his wife, Savannah James, has used her o.
articles.body: LeBron James has spent years in the spotlight as one of the biggest names in sports. Away from the NBA court, his wife, Savannah James, has used her own platform to talk about issues that go well beyond basketball. On February 27, 2026, Savannah’s conversation on “Everybody’s Crazy” turned to men’s mental health and why some men still struggle to speak openly about what they are going through.Her message was direct. Talking about mental health should not make a man feel weak. Savannah James explains why some men see mental health as a “weak point”During a recent episode of Everybody’s Crazy, Savannah James and co-host April McDaniel spoke with caller Christopher Rivera Mannon about vulnerability and the pressure men can feel when discussing their mental health.Savannah explained that some men may worry that opening up will make them look less strong. She said the problem can start with the way society treats emotional vulnerability, especially when men feel expected to handle everything on their own.“I think it also is guys talking about mental health seems like it's not cool or it doesn't feel like you're strong enough and that is not true, and some guys don't want to, they feel like it's a weak point,” Savannah said during the discussion.That comment became the heart of the conversation. Savannah pointed out how easily men can talk about their jobs, families and children, yet struggle to turn the conversation toward themselves.For someone like LeBron James, who has spent much of his life dealing with enormous public expectations, the subject also carries a familiar theme: the pressure to stay composed even when life gets difficult. Savannah did not make the discussion about her husband, though. Instead, she focused on a wider issue facing men.She and McDaniel also discussed the idea of men having trusted groups where they can speak honestly, similar to the close support systems many women have.The conversation then moved toward what vulnerability can actually mean. April McDaniel says asking for help can be a sign of strengthMcDaniel challenged the idea that showing vulnerability takes away from a man's strength. She argued that being honest and admitting when help is needed can take real courage.“Yes. And I think the strongest way that you can be is vulnerable and honest, and like when you need help, ask for help,” McDaniel said during the same “Everybody’s Crazy” episode.She also highlighted the need for more therapists of color, both men and women. McDaniel said some people want professional help but struggle to find support that feels accessible to them.That added another layer to Savannah’s point. The issue is not simply getting men to talk. They also need spaces where those conversations feel safe and useful.Savannah James’ message was ultimately simple. Men should not have to choose between appearing strong and admitting that they are struggling. Her intelligent conversation pushed back on that old idea and placed vulnerability in a different light.Instead of seeing mental health conversations as a weakness, Savannah and McDaniel argued that asking for help can be part of taking care of yourself.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El muro más alto: "No tenemos miedo de nadie"
articles.standfirst: España juega este sábado la semifinal del Mundial femenino ante EEUU (20.00)
articles.summary: España juega este sábado la semifinal del Mundial femenino ante EEUU (20.00)
articles.body: En 2022 España no acudió al Mundial de Sidney. Fue el segundo gran torneo que se perdía en el siglo XXI tras los Juegos de Londres 2012. La ausencia en el Mundial fue la consecuencia de un ciclo fallido y la razón por la que sólo una jugadora del actual plantel, Alba Torrens, tuviera partidos en Mundiales antes de comenzar el torneo de Berlín. Tras no ir al Mundial, España inició, ya lo había hecho antes, un proceso de cambio generacional que poco a poco fue dando frutos, dos platas europeas y un quinto puesto en los Juegos, hasta llegar al presente equipo que, cuatro años después de su ausencia, está en unas semifinales del Mundial. El ascenso de nuevo a la élite es evidente. El trabajo de formación de los clubes y, sobre todo, de la Federación española recoge ahora la recompensa de estar entre las cuatro mejores selecciones del planeta. Y no hay excusas, todas las que están han tendo muchas dificultades con la preparación de este torneo. Este equipo, el de Miguel Méndez, es un devorador de retos, pero esta vez tiene uno delante de tamaño descomunal, gigante como su rival. Este sábado se las verá con Estados Unidos a partir de las 20.00 horas en el Uber Arena. El premio de ese partido, además de la gloria, es la final del Mundial del domingo. Complicado encontrar un escenerio mejor para una hazaña de las españolas. Pero este es un equipo que no debe medir por el valor de la recompensa final. Pase lo que pase desde hoy han alcanzado el éxito en Berlín. Tanto por la propuesta de su juego, algo en lo que Méndez y la FEB llevan años trabajando, como por el ambiente del equipo, envidia de otras selecciones. Destilan simpatía, amistad, ganas de disfrutar jugando y de pasárselo muy bien. Sólo se puede llegar lejos con esos ingredientes. Aunque el reto sea mayúsculo porque EEUU lleva casi 20 años sin perder un sólo partido internacional y con un balance que asusta (73-0), España va a aslir a por el partido, como decía el seleccionador: "Lo vamos a preparar para ir a ganar, como hacemos siempre", y con un plan: "Trataremos de esconder nuestras debilidades y de sacar partido de las suyas". En el vestuario, hay mucha confianza de estar ante un momento único en la historia. Awa Fam, una de las imágenes de esta selección, analilzaba para MARCA el partido: "Sabemos el equipo que tenemos enfrente, son jugadoras con mucho talento, pero no vamos a salir con miedo. Queremos salir a competir y si podemos, a superarlas. Sabemos que para ganar tenemos que poner todo lo mejor de cada una a la vez en la pista, que nos salga el partido. Pero sobre todo, no tenerles miedo". A EEUU se le han visto debilidades. Tiene mucho puntos fuertes, pero se han visto carencias y fisuras que no había en otros equipos estadounidenses: "Hablamos de ello sí", reconocía Awa. "Es una forma de creernos que podemos ganarles. Sabemos que tenemos que estar casi por encima de nuestro nivel, pero eso otros años no servía. Yo creo que si hacemos nuestro juego, tendremos opciones". La pívot española, que conoce bien el equipo estadounidense porque juega en la WNBA (Seattle Storm), da algunas pistas sobre cómo tumbar al gigante: "No tenemos que dejar que corran ni que tengan segundas opciones. Italia eso lo hizo bien y casi le sale. Tenemos que rebotear y ser valientos yendo al aro, que sientan que no tenemos miedo. Creo que al final lo importante es hacer nuestro juego". Aunque ninguna jugadora de EEUU esté haciendo un torneo redondo, hay algunos nombres a tener muy en cuenta. Para Awa Fam: "Breanna Stewart es la estrella y un poco la jugadora que puede hacer de todo. Y Chelsea Gary me encanta, creo que es una de las mejores bases de nuestra Liga, como Caitlin Clark. Tienen muchas jugadoras muy buenas". Awa, a pesar de la distancia, dice que puede sentir el calor de todo un país detrás apoyando a su selección: “Es increíble ver todos los mensajes que recibimos, la gente que viene aquí solo a vernos, todos los que están allí en España pendientes. Solo les puedo decir que haremos todo lo posible por ganar”. La selección femenina de vuelta a la élite Mundial tiene ante sí uno de esos retos que se presentan pocas veces en la vida. Ante la EEUU más terrenal de los últimos años, se disputa un puesto en la gran final del domingo. Para una generación de jugadoras es cruzar las puertas de la gloria. Es el Muro más alto que tienen que derribar.

articles.title: ‘Not as a…’ Nikola Jokic once revealed how he wants his kids to remember him
articles.summary: Nikola Jokic is one of the greatest basketball players to ever play the game. However, he once explained that’s not how he wants his children to think of him...
articles.body:
Nikola Jokic is one of the greatest basketball players to ever play the game. However, he once explained that's not how he wants his children to think of him.

Nikola Jokic has changed the game of basketball over the course of his career. The Denver Nuggets superstar has won three MVPs and a Finals MVP to go along with a championship, too.

Jokic's accomplishments on the court are almost too numerous to count. He is a triple-double machine despite being a big man, something that no one before him has managed at the highest level.

The Serbian has never been one to big himself up or act like he's doing something extraordinary. And despite all his achievements, Jokic would prefer for his own children to remember him differently.

Nikola Jokic would rather his children remembered him as a father than a basketball star

Jokic has two children with his wife, Natalija, a daughter born in 2021 and a son born in 2024. And the 31-year-old cares a lot more about life off the court than he does on it.

Speaking on a podcast in 2023, Jokic explained how he wanted to be remembered and what he values. That take recently resurfaced on social media.

"I really, when I finish my career, I really wish nobody knows me," Jokic said. "And I really wish my kid, or kids in the future, really remember me as a dad, not as a basketball player."

"That's going to be my goal in life… Just to live in the moment, be a normal person. Go drink with your buddy, go have lunch, go play with the kid, go drive horses and nobody's going to make a big deal of that."

The NBA superstar's words from back then provide a lot of insight into who he is as a person. Having said that, it's not going to stop Jokic from amassing many more accolades before his career ends.

articles.title: Cheap NBA Free Agents Who Can Still Help Every Team
articles.summary: With NBA training camps right around the corner, focus has firmly shifted from potential transactions to crucial topics such as position battles, overall rotations, player development and, of course, #musclewatch.
articles.body:
With NBA training camps right around the corner, focus has firmly shifted from potential transactions to crucial topics such as position battles, overall rotations, player development and, of course, #musclewatch.

Still, much like basketball itself, free agency never sleeps.

A handful of potentially useful names continue to float around the open market, just waiting for an opportunity to deepen a squad's bench. This one's for them.

None of these names should cost more than a minimum contract. Some, if not all, could be convinced to accept non-guaranteed training-camp deals. That makes them gettable for every team.

Members of this list are being selected on the merits of basketball intrigue. Vets who will draw interest predominantly for their locker-room presence (i.e., Kevin Love) are not included.

The same goes for anyone who needs to dominate the ball or play a hyper-specific role. Cam Thomas might be worth a dice roll for some team, but these five free agents are candidates to help any team.

2025-26 Stats: 6.7 PTS, 2.3 REB, 0.8 AST, 0.4 STL

Generally speaking, it's never a good sign when a lottery pick doesn't get tendered a qualifying offer by his incumbent team and instead has his rights entirely renounced. Those are the circumstances under which Ochai Agbaji finds himself.

The skepticism among teams is understandable. Agbaji is enough of an offensive non-factor that his team might end up running four-versus-five in the half-court.

Still, standing 6'5", the combo wing has routinely proved his defensive mettle. He has ranked no lower than the 87th percentile in matchup difficulty since entering the league and has spent more than two-thirds of his career possessions guarding primary ball-handlers, according to BBall Index.

Any squad in need of a perimeter defensive punch should have his name atop their late-summer whiteboard Post-It ranch dressing-stained dinner napkin.

Worst-case scenario, they burn a minimum deal on someone who can't crack the rotation. Best-case scenario, Agbaji rewinds the clock to 2023 (35.5 percent) or 2025 (39.9 percent), when he actually connected on a "Hey, we can play him!" share of 200-plus three-point attempts.

2025-26 Stats: 7.9 PTS, 3.9 REB, 2.1 AST, 1.0 STL

Bruce Brown Jr. no longer profiles as a glittery defender and Sixth Man of the Year candidate, but he still has the juice of a medium-rent gap-filler.

Buying into his 38.5 percent clip from deep last season is tough. He's a career 34.4 percent marksman from behind the rainbow who's eclipsed 35 percent for an entire year just three times. But if his outlier showing in 2025-26 isn't proof of evolution, it at least shows what can happen when he takes mostly unguarded shots.

None of Brown's other connective skills are a mirage. He keeps the ball moving. He can reach the basket on or off the rock. He knows how to cut and relocate in the half-court. And he keeps defenses guessing from short-roll territory.

2025-26 Stats: 2.4 PTS, 0.7 REB, 0.5 AST, 0.2 STL

Through five years at the NBA level, Lindy Waters III has seldom been a regular part of any team's rotation. After a half-decade of bouncing around, now would be an understandable time to give up on that ever-changing situation.

High-volume shooting is always useful to have in the tank. Waters promises it in spades.

Among everyone who's logged at least as much floor time over the past five seasons, the 6'5" shooting guard is one of six players tossing up more than 10 three-point attempts per 36 minutes. He is joined by Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson, LaMelo Ball, Sam Merrill and Buddy Hield.

Although Waters' efficiency isn't what you'd call scintillating, he's downed a passable 36.3 percent of his triples during this span. That's a value add, given he's not consigned to standalone opportunities in the corners.

Waters has never ranked lower than the 86th percentile in off-ball screening touches per 75 possessions, according to BBall Index. That kind of usage puts constant pressure on opposing defenses—and any team could use it.

2025-26 Stats: 9.2 PTS, 2.8 REB, 0.7 AST, 0.7 STL

Cam Whitmore finds himself without a team after the Washington Wizards flipped him to the Cleveland Cavaliers, who subsequently waived him. His availability is just the latest development in one of the strangest early-career arcs we've seen.

Selected 20th overall by the Houston Rockets in 2023, Whitmore's scoring, shooting and downhill pedigree initially made him look like a steal. But his role in H-Town evaporated as a sophomore, and he was shipped to Washington ahead of last season.

The Wizards gave Whitmore a crack at minutes to begin the year, but head coach Brian Keefe benched him for a dearth of passing and disengaged defense . Doctors then found a blood clot in his right shoulder that sidelined him the rest of the year.

This is all to say: Whitmore clearly comes with baggage. But a 6'7" wing with a(n admittedly brief) history of attacking the rim and shooting threes is always worth a flier. The appeal skyrockets knowing he just turned 22 in July.

For all his flaws, Whitmore is instant offense. He's averaging over 20 points per 36 minutes for his career. Out of everyone from his draft class who's seen as much court time, Victor Wembanyama, Brandon Miller, Keyonte George and Brice Sensabaugh are the only other players doing the same .

2025-26 Stats: 8.0 PTS, 4.0 REB, 4.4 AST, 0.8 STL

Vince Williams Jr. is recovering from a torn ACL in his left knee and is bound to miss a huge chunk of the 2026-27 campaign. A smart team will consider getting in on the ground floor of his return rather than competing for his services this winter or next offseason.

Serious injuries are never a good time, but ACL tears aren't considered career-altering these days. Williams could resume killing defensive possessions once he gets enough game reps under his belt.

Much of his value is also rooted in guarding up. That's more of a strength factor than an athleticism variable.

Touch-and-go three-point shooting is the bigger concern. The 36.8 percent clip he posted last year in limited action on catch-and-fire triples was the second-highest of his career.

That shouldn't deter playoff teams in need of leveling up their defense who have the depth to navigate the regular season largely without him, or squads prepared to grab him now with the thought of negotiating in a club option and eyeing a next-season timeline.

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: OutKick's Craig Carton reveals the real reason Nike stock is in the tank: 'They're failing miserably'
articles.summary: Craig Carton traces Nike's downfall from its Colin Kaepernick partnership to the Dylan Mulvaney sports bra campaign that replaced Brandi Chastain.
articles.body: In case you've been living under a rock these past few days, Nike has had a rough time this week. Between the unveiling of their universally reviled "Specter Edition" NBA jerseys to their stock taking a nosedive, the company that was once seen as unsinkable is starting to take on water. Things have gotten so bad for Nike that they're set to be booted from the S&P 100, a sign that the company is trending in the wrong direction. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! OutKick's Craig Carton, a self-admitted "Nike man," thinks he knows what the issue is, and if you've been paying attention, it shouldn't come as a shock to you. "This is part of the problem right here," Carton says as he points at a picture of the aforementioned Specter Edition jerseys. "Nike decided, apparently, to hire a blind creator to basically pull a Jackson Pollock and just start ramming paint at the wall." If you've seen the jerseys, Carton is spot on. I've likened them to a Windows screensaver from the 90s that has been ripped from a dying computer monitor, but Jackson Pollock is a solid pull as well. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "Part of the reason for Nike's downfall is garbage like this," he explains. But, as Carton alludes to, it's only part of the problem. The other half of the issue is more historical. "In 2018, Nike decided to get in bed with Colin Kaepernick," Carton recounts. "And they scrapped 'Just Do It' and they started a new slogan, which was 'Dream Crazy.'" "The only thing crazy that they did was partner with a lunatic who hates America." Carton's point is well received, and anyone who had any sort of foresight could have predicted that once the "woke" fad — which is all it was in the first place — died down, it would no longer be trendy to partner with these characters from the lunatic fringe. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Nike did so anyway, and now the proverbial chickens have come home to roost. It doesn't stop there, though, as Carton continues to explain Nike's follies, citing their pulling of the Betsy Ross Edition shoes in 2019 per Kaepernick's request. Then, in 2020, a slogan change from "Just Do It" to "Don't Do It" in the wake of the George Floyd protests further sealed the fate of the athletic apparel giant. "So the slogan that made Nike popular... they decided to do the exact opposite by starting a new slogan," says Carton. Finally, in 2023, Nike made the same mistake Bud Light made by deciding to partner with trans influencer Dylan Mulvaney, destroying a decades-long campaign with Brandi Chastain as the centerpiece of their sports bra ads. "They made Dylan Mulvaney the face of their sports bra program," Carton explained. "They took this amazing, unique moment in the history of women's sports, and they bastardized it by bringing it to a transgender woman." Carton is, of course, referring to the moment in the 1999 Women's World Cup, when Chastain scored the game-winning goal in the Cup Final and removed her jersey to reveal she was wearing a Nike sports bra. If anyone in the marketing offices at Nike is still confused as to why their stock keeps plummeting, send them this clip. articles.title: El ‘caso DeJulius’ acaba en negocio redondo para el UCAM Murcia
articles.standfirst: Recibe una compensación económica del Besiktas por su cesión y el próximo verano recupera los derechos sobre el jugador, al que sube su cláusula de salida
articles.summary: Recibe una compensación económica del Besiktas por su cesión y el próximo verano recupera los derechos sobre el jugador, al que sube su cláusula de salida
articles.body: David DeJulius se marcha al Besiktas, pero el UCAM Murcia no sale perdiendo. El base estadounidense nacionalizado eslovaco abandona el club murciano rumbo a Turquía pese a haber renovado hasta 2028, aunque lo hará finalmente en calidad de cedido y a cambio de una compensación económica. El UCAM, además, recuperará el próximo verano los derechos sobre el jugador. Y hay más: si DeJulius no continúa entonces en Murcia, el club cobrará una cláusula de rescisión que, además, ha sido incrementada. Pierde al jugador, sí, pero el negocio puede acabar siendo redondo. El base, de 27 años y natural de Detroit, llegó el pasado verano procedente del Bursaspor y se convirtió en una de las grandes sensaciones de la Liga Endesa. Firmó 17,67 puntos por partido, segundo máximo anotador de la competición, y fue incluido en el mejor quinteto de la temporada. El conflicto arrancó después de que el UCAM anunciara su renovación el 6 de marzo. A mediados de julio, DeJulius comunicó su intención de no cumplir el contrato y regresó a Turquía, provocando la denuncia del club ante el Tribunal de Arbitraje de la FIBA y el posterior proceso judicial. Ahora, el acuerdo devuelve la pelota al tejado murciano: dinero en el bolsillo y los derechos del jugador de vuelta el próximo verano.
