articles.title: Florida Guard Denzel Aberdeen Sues the NCAA In Hopes of Gaining a Fifth Year of Eligibility
articles.summary: GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Florida guard Denzel Aberdeen has joined a growing list of players suing the NCAA in hopes of gaining a fifth year of eligibility.
articles.body:
GAINESVILLE, Fla. (AP) — Florida guard Denzel Aberdeen has joined a growing list of players suing the NCAA in hopes of gaining a fifth year of eligibility.

Aberdeen's attorney, Jesse Panuccio, filed the lawsuit Friday in Gainesville. His motion notes that more than 30 courts across the country have ruled that the NCAA's "arbitrary decision" against student-athletes who began college careers during the 2022-23 season and completed four seasons of eligibility is "unlawful."

"The NCAA's refusal to honor its current eligibility framework breaches its contract with UF, which is intended to benefit student-athletes like Aberdeen," the suit said.

The NCAA's move to a five-year, age-based eligibility model has led to a series of court fights across the country.

Aberdeen played three seasons at Florida before transferring to Kentucky last year. He reenrolled at Florida earlier this year in hopes of finishing his undergraduate degree. He has worked out and practiced with the Gators all summer.

He initially planned to convince the NCAA that his freshman year in Gainesville should be considered a redshirt season. The 6-foot-5 Orlando native played just 12 games in 2022-23, scoring 19 points in 41 total minutes. He had hoped to get a waiver from the NCAA to secure another year of eligibility.

But the NCAA has since adopted the five-year eligibility model, which is scheduled to be fully implemented next fall, that will allow players to have five years of eligibility with the clock starting when athletes turn 19 or graduate from high school, whichever is earlier.

That change quickly led to lawsuits from four-year players in the high school class of 2022, like Aberdeen.

As of last week, the NCAA said there have been 79 lawsuits with a total of 450 plaintiffs across all sports involved in litigation tied to the five-year rule, with 234 of those coming in men's basketball and 33 in women's basketball. Of that group, 154 men's players and 26 women's players have received some type of relief from the courts allowing them to play while the rest are currently ineligible.

If granted a temporary restraining order, Aberdeen would slide into a starting spot to replace Xaivian Lee.

The Gators already are the betting favorite — and likely to be ranked No. 1 in preseason polls — to win it all in 2027. Coach Todd Golden retained most of last year's roster, most notably big men Alex Condon, Thomas Haugh and Rueben Chinyelu.

Aberdeen started 35 games for Kentucky last season, averaging 13.5 points, 3.4 assists and 2.5 rebounds. He came off the bench the previous two years at Florida and averaged 7.7 points as a junior in 2024-25.

articles.title: La imparable bajada a los infiernos del AS Monaco: ¡sin garantías para jugar en Tercera División!
articles.standfirst: La Federación Francesa de Baloncesto asegura que "no ha sido capaz de presentar un expediente que justifique la veracidad y fiabilidad de su situación financiera"
articles.summary: La Federación Francesa de Baloncesto asegura que "no ha sido capaz de presentar un expediente que justifique la veracidad y fiabilidad de su situación financiera"
articles.body: El AS Monaco Basket (ASM), vigente campeón de Francia y finalista de la Euroliga en 2025, no ha logrado ni siquiera su inscripción en la tercera división francesa debido a la falta de garantías financieras que ya habían supuesto su vertiginoso descenso desde la primera. En un comunicado, la Federación Francesa de Baloncesto (FFB) siguió las conclusiones de su Comisión de Control de Gestión (CCG) -encargada de auditar la situación financiera de los clubes- y confirmó que quedó constatado que el ASM "no ha sido capaz de presentar un expediente que justifique la veracidad y fiabilidad de la situación financiera de la sociedad". La FFB agregó que tampoco se dan las condiciones para aplicar al club garantías suficientes para justificar "una medida de excepción" e integrarlo en la tercera. El AS Monaco Basket había pedido jugar en esa categoría debido a los graves problemas de deuda que arrastra y que le han impedido inscribirse en el baloncesto profesional. A pesar de sus excelentes resultados deportivos, el ASM fue excluido de la Betclic Élite y de la Élite 2 el pasado 3 de julio tras el examen de su caso por el órgano de control financiero (DNCCG) de la Liga Nacional de Baloncesto (LNB), el gendarme de las finanzas de los clubes. La Eurocup también oficializó la expulsión del club de las competiciones europeas. El motivo son los 24 millones de euros de deuda acumulada durante la gestión del magnate ruso Alexey Fedorychev debido al alto presupuesto del equipo en esa etapa por su elevada masa salarial. Ni siquiera el plan de rescate liderado por el exjugador de la NBA Jamal Mashburn ha sido, de momento, suficiente para convencer a las autoridades de la solvencia del ASM. El AS Monaco Basket ha sido uno de los clubes punteros en Europa durante la última década. Además de finalista de la Euroliga en 2025, fue tercero en 2023 en ese mismo torneo y vencedor de la Eurocopa en 2021. En Francia, ganó las Ligas de 2023, 2024 y 2026. El Bosna Sarajevo bosnio reemplazó en la Eurocopa 2026-2027 al Mónaco.

Former UNC Charlotte Athletic Director Mike Hill is joining the NCAA to lead men's basketball, including March Madness and the Final Four.

In March, former Clemson Deputy Athletic Director Kevin White replaced Hill.

articles.title: El Real Madrid, a punto de fichar a un excompañero de LeBron y Doncic
articles.standfirst: Nick Smith Jr., exterior de 1,88 m y 22 años con pasado en la NBA tras jugar en Lakers y Hornets, el elegido para reforzar el perímetro
articles.summary: Nick Smith Jr., exterior de 1,88 m y 22 años con pasado en la NBA tras jugar en Lakers y Hornets, el elegido para reforzar el perímetro
articles.body: El Real Madrid llevaba semanas peinando el mercado en busca de un jugador de perímetro polivalente con el que poder cerrar con garantías todos los puestos de su plantilla y el elegido parece ser Nick Smith Jr., exterior de 1,88 m y 22 años con pasado en la NBA tras jugar en Lakers y Hornets. y que estaría a punto de firmar por el conjunto blanco según adelanta el periodista Chema de Lucas. Era la asignatura pendiente del proyecto madridista para cerrar una plantilla de relumbrón con la que poder aspirar a todos los títulos tras una temporada en blanco. Tras quedarse por el camino este verano otros jugadores que estuvieron en su radar, como Nadir Hifi (París Basketball), Lonnie Walker IV (Nuggets) o Armoni Brooks (Valencia Basket), el club parece haber dado con el jugador idóneo que encaja en las características que buscaba. El perfil de Smith Jr. es especialmente atractivo por su edad y por el margen de crecimiento. Nacido el 18 de abril de 2004 en Jacksonville (Arkansas), mide 1,88 metros y puede actuar tanto de base como de escolta. Brilló en su época del instituto —número uno nacional de su promoción— y llegó a Arkansas como uno de los grandes talentos de Estados Unidos. En su único año universitario, condicionado por una lesión de rodilla que le hizo perderse 19 partidos, promedió 12,5 puntos, 1,6 rebotes y 1,7 asistencias en sólo 17 encuentros. Charlotte apostó por él con el número 27 del Draft de 2023, en la primera ronda, confiando en un anotador al que la propia franquicia veía capaz de desenvolverse en las dos posiciones exteriores. En sus dos temporadas con los Hornets disputó 111 partidos, 27 como titular, con medias globales de 8,0 puntos, 1,8 rebotes y 1,8 asistencias, aunque su segunda campaña dejó mejores sensaciones: 9,9 puntos, 2,1 rebotes y 2,4 asistencias en 60 partidos, con un 34% de acierto en triples y un espectacular 93,5% desde la línea de tiros libres. Su salto a los Lakers le permitió compartir vestuario con estrellas como LeBron James y Luka Doncic. En la temporada 2025-26 disputó 30 partidos con Los Ángeles, con 6,2 puntos y un 39,5% en triples, antes de convertirse en agente libre. Además, tuvo un notable impacto en la G League, donde alcanzó 19,7 puntos, 3,5 rebotes y 5,7 asistencias de media en los tres partidos registrados con los South Bay Lakers. Su mejor actuación NBA llegó precisamente con los Lakers, cuando anotó 25 puntos, con 5 de 6 en triples y seis asistencias ante Portland. Si finalmente aterriza en Madrid, Pedro Martínez tendría en sus manos un exterior joven, explosivo y con capacidad para generarse sus propios tiros, aunque podría necesitar de un tiempo para adaptarse al baloncesto europeo, y también mejorar su regularidad y pulir su talento en la dirección para el baloncesto continental, distinto al que él ha conocido hasta ahora.

articles.body:
Chicago Bulls guard Norman Powell isn't buying into the hype around the Los Angeles Lakers after their flurry of offseason moves to overhaul their roster.

Appearing on a recent live stream with N3on, Powell named the Lakers as his most overrated team in the NBA.

The Lakers added Walker Kessler, Quentin Grimes, Sandro Mamukelashvili and Collin Sexton to play alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves.

That's plenty of new faces to incorporate, with Kessler potentially being the biggest X-factor as a lob threat on offense for Dončić and a defensive stopper in the paint. If the moves pay off, the ceiling is high for the Lakers.

The problem, though, is even with a high ceiling, the Lakers have to go through the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference if they want to reach the NBA Finals.

articles.title: Francia no falla y se mete en la final del Mundial
articles.standfirst: Gana a Alemania y jugará por el oro por primera vez en su historia
articles.summary: Gana a Alemania y jugará por el oro por primera vez en su historia
articles.body: Francia mantiene la velocidad de crucero que lleva en todo el Mundial. Eso sí, ante Alemania tuvo más oleaje del habitual, se encontró con un partido más incómodo y por primera vez en el campeonato tuvo que trabajar más de la cuenta. Pero no se podía esperar otra cosa de una semifinal que ganó 86-64, para colarse en la final que aspira a ganar. Con un abarrotado Uber Arena empujando (12.650 espectadores, todo vendido), Alemania plantó cara con el orgullo del anfitrión. Llegaron a pensar en la sorpresa, pero cada vez que las alemanas anotaban de dos o tres, Francia tenía una respuesta. Las galas, apoyadas en el tridente formado por Salaun, Johannes y, sobre todo Gabby Williams (puro talento), fueron abriendo hueco mientras mermaban la resistencia germana. En Francia la fuerza la puede poner Salaun o Malonga, la velocidad Leite, y el cerebro Johannes, pero el baloncesto, el talento, lo pone Gabby Williams que es absolutamente diferencial en el baloncesto FIBA. Sujetó al equipo en el exigente primer tiempo, cuando Francia sólo se llevó el primer cuarto por dos puntos, 25-23, y se fue el descanso con su segunda peor anotación en 20 minutos en el Mundial, 45-38. Sólo había anotado menos en una primera parte ante Corea, 43. Llamaba la atención los muchos fallos bajo canasta del equipo francés en situaciones muy claras. El equipo francés suele salir del descanso a toda velocidad para romper los partidos. Lo intentó con un 7-0 de salida (52-38) que amenazaba con llevarse por delante la semifinal antes de tiempo. No lo permitió Alemania que volvió al choque con un 0-5 (54-45), aunque en los últimos minutos del tercer acto, las galas volvieron a marcharse, 64-50 con una canasta sobre la bocina de Toure para igualar la máxima hasta ese momento. Los recursos franceses afloraron cuando en un pequeño arreón comprimieron el marcador (69-60) a cinco minutos para el final del partido. Defensa más agresiva, ideas más claras en ataque y la ventaja volvía a crecer (78-64 a 3:14). Las ilusiones alemanas menguaban con el paso de los segundos y las canastas francesas. Un triple y un robo de Johannes (81-74) enterraron definitivamente las esperanzas del anfitrión. Williams se fue hasta los 22 puntos, Salaun hizo 14 y Johannes 13. En Alemania, que acabó ovacionada, brillaron Guelich y Sabally, 12 puntos cada una. Francia jugará la final del Mundial este domingo (20.00) con todas las opciones de llevarse el oro. Será su primera final del Mundial y ya ha ganado su segunda medalla tras el bronce de 1953. En Berlín ha sido el mejor equipo del torneo hasta ahora. Alemania por su parte superó sus expectativas cuando ganó a Bélgica y le queda la lucha por la medalla de bronce este domingo (16.30), sabiendo que ha estado por encima de lo esperado.

articles.title: “I am incredibly proud to be..”: How Stephen Curry backed Unrivaled when it was still finding its feet before the women’s basketball league surged to a $650 million valuation
articles.summary: NBA News: Stephen Curry made his Unrivaled investment in March 2025, when the women’s 3-on-3 league was still in its early days. More than a year later, the dec.
articles.body: Stephen Curry made his Unrivaled investment in March 2025, when the women’s 3-on-3 league was still in its early days. More than a year later, the decision looks far bigger. Unrivaled has grown into a major name in women’s basketball, and its latest funding round has pushed its valuation to $650 million.The change did not happen overnight. Curry joined a group of investors who backed the league because of its different approach to women’s basketball, particularly its focus on giving players a stake in what they helped build. Why Stephen Curry backed Unrivaled and its player-first approach?When Stephen Curry joined Unrivaled in March 2025, the league had already attracted major names from sports and entertainment. Its investor group included Giannis Antetokounmpo, Coco Gauff, Alex Morgan, Dawn Staley, Michael Phelps and Carmelo Anthony. Unrivaled had also raised $35 million through its seed and Series A rounds.The league came from WNBA stars Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier, who launched Unrivaled with a simple idea: create a new professional basketball product while giving players a meaningful share in the business.That part clearly caught the NBA legends attention.“I am incredibly proud to be joining the Unrivaled family as the league continues to set a new standard for how women’s professional sports should operate,” Curry said in a statement sent to Unrivaled on March 12, 2025. He added that the league was changing not only how basketball could be played, but also how athletes could be valued and invested in.That made Curry's role more interesting than a celebrity putting money into another sports venture. He was backing a league built around athlete ownership. Unrivaled gives players equity opportunities alongside salaries and benefits, keeping players at the center of the business model.And that model has grown considerably. By August 2026, Unrivaled said its player equity pool had climbed to nearly $200 million. Players also remained the league's largest equity group.For Stephen Curry, the investment also connected with his wider interest in growing the game beyond the NBA. Instead of simply attaching his name to women's basketball, he became part of the investor group helping Unrivaled build its own business. From $35 million in funding to a $650 million valuationThe numbers now show just how far Unrivaled has come. On Aug. 26, 2026, the league announced that its Series C funding round had passed its original $100 million target and pushed its valuation to $650 million. The round came after Unrivaled reached a $340 million valuation in September 2025.The league also started reaching larger audiences. On January 30, 2026, its Philadelphia stop drew 21,490 fans to Xfinity Mobile Arena, setting the venue's attendance record and the record for a regular-season professional women's basketball game.Unrivaled is now preparing for its third season, which begins in January 2027. The league has expanded to eight clubs and 54 players, while continuing to build its presence outside Miami.Stephen Curry made his investment when Unrivaled was still proving what it could become. Now, the $650 million valuation and growing crowds offer a clear look at the scale of the bet he made.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kate Koval signs with Baylor after receiving NCAA waiver to transfer from LSU
articles.summary: The Ukrainian native left LSU in August after Tigers head coach signed Russian center Anna Minaeva.
articles.body:
Kate Koval has signed with Baylor days after being granted a waiver by the NCAA to enter the transfer portal. The Ukrainian native left LSU in August after Tigers head coach Kim Mulkey signed Russian center Anna Minaeva. Koval cited the ongoing Russian-Ukrainian war as the reason for her exit from LSU.

"We are beyond excited to welcome Kate to Baylor," said Baylor head coach Nicki Collen . "She has played at an elite level over the last two seasons and has shown the consistent ability to score around the rim and protect the rim. Kate, at 6-5, can be a decision maker on the perimeter both as a scorer and facilitator, which will expand our offense. Her shot-blocking ability will help anchor our defense. She is an elite student with a big heart for others, and our fans will love her on and off the court."

Koval was allowed to enter the transfer portal and compete immediately under a " legislative relief waiver ." Such a waiver is granted beyond a sport-specific transfer window due to an "exigent event outside the student-athlete's control unrelated to athletics opportunities or participation at their current institution that demands the student-athlete's immediate departure from the institution."

In a social media post earlier this month, Koval wrote that she intended to return to LSU for the 2026-27 season until she learned that Minaeva had been recruited to the team by Mulkey.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract," wrote Koval, whose father serves in the Ukrainian military and has been part of the war since Russia invaded the country in 2022. "People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes."

Koval said she was told by Mulkey, who coached Baylor from 2000 to 2021, of the signing "several days" after the closing of the transfer portal window on April 20. That made the center "question whether LSU remained the right place for me."

Koval began her collegiate career at Notre Dame before transferring to LSU last season. She averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds and started 17 games for the Tigers, while shooting 56% from the field and helping the team reach the Sweet 16.

The Bears went 25-9 last season and finished third in the Big 12. They exited the NCAA tournament in the second round for the fourth time in five seasons.

articles.summary: Baylor signed Ukrainian center Kate Koval, the school announced Saturday, several weeks after she left LSU because Tigers coach Kim Mulkey brought in a Russian player.
articles.body:
Baylor signed Ukrainian center Kate Koval, the school announced Saturday, several weeks after she left LSU because Tigers coach Kim Mulkey brought in a Russian player.

Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and the two countries have been at war since.

Koval was allowed to enter the transfer portal outside of the normal window after she was granted a legislative relief waiver by the NCAA that was approved earlier this week, according to a person familiar with the situation. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak publicly about it.

"We are beyond excited to welcome Kate to Baylor," Bears coach Nicki Collen said in a statement. "She has played at an elite level over the last two seasons and has shown the consistent ability to score around the rim and protect the rim. Kate, at 6-foot-5, can be a decision maker on the perimeter both as a scorer and facilitator, which will expand our offense. Her shot-blocking ability will help anchor our defense. She is an elite student with a big heart for others, and our fans will love her on and off the court."

Koval had posted on social media last week about her decision to leave LSU . Now she'll be at the school that Mulkey turned into a women's basketball powerhouse before leaving to coach the Tigers.

"For me, this war is not distant or abstract," Koval wrote . "People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes.

"The timing of this situation and the deeply personal effect it has had on me, my family, and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me. This decision has not been easy. While I understand and respect that roster decisions are a part of college basketball. I have to remain true to myself, my values, and my country."

Koval averaged 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.2 blocks last season for the Tigers. She started her college career at Notre Dame and averaged 5.3 points and 4.7 rebounds in the 2024-25 season.

articles.title: Maledon y Luwawu-Cabarrot lideran la paliza del Real Madrid al Unicaja
articles.standfirst: Los de Pedro Martínez, con un ataque demoledor, conquistan el Torneo Costa del Sol (74-113)
articles.summary: Los de Pedro Martínez, con un ataque demoledor, conquistan el Torneo Costa del Sol (74-113)
articles.body: El Real Madrid se proclamó campeón del Torneo Costa del Sol tras pasar por encima del Unicaja (74-113) en un partido que quedó sentenciado en el segundo cuarto. El conjunto de Pedro Martínez convirtió el duelo en un ejercicio de superioridad después de un primer periodo de máxima intensidad, en el que Cameron Hunt fue el gran protagonista del equipo malagueño. El estadounidense sostuvo a los cajistas con 13 de los primeros 20 puntos y despertó al Carpena con su electricidad y capacidad ofensiva. El escenario cambió radicalmente tras el primer cuarto, que terminó con ventaja local (27-25). El Real Madrid salió disparado en el segundo acto y firmó un demoledor parcial de 9-30. Campazzo tomó el mando con siete puntos consecutivos y, a partir de ahí, los blancos encontraron soluciones por todas partes. Tavares castigó en la pintura, la defensa elevó varias marchas y el Unicaja comenzó a acumular errores. Ni los tiempos muertos de Vidorreta pudieron frenar a un equipo que llegó al descanso con 19 puntos de ventaja (36-55). El guion apenas varió tras el paso por vestuarios. El Real Madrid mantuvo un ritmo altísimo y continuó ampliando la diferencia hasta alcanzar el +28 al final del tercer cuarto (52-80). Luwawu-Cabarrot y Maledon disfrutaron especialmente en ataque, mientras que en el Unicaja destacó la resistencia de Perry y las buenas acciones de Hunt. También dejó detalles interesantes Melvin Pantzar, en un encuentro que sirvió para seguir acumulando minutos de preparación de cara al inicio oficial de la temporada. El último cuarto terminó de confirmar la exhibición madridista. Movilidad, acierto y una circulación de balón propia de un equipo mucho más rodado fueron demasiado para un Unicaja claramente inferior físicamente. Maledon lideró a los blancos con 19 puntos, seguido de Luwawu-Cabarrot (16) y Campazzo (15), mientras que Perry y Hunt fueron los máximos anotadores cajistas con 11 puntos. El Real Madrid repitió así la contundencia mostrada ante Baskonia y cerró el Costa del Sol con otra victoria por casi 40 puntos. Para el Unicaja, toca seguir trabajando para construir su propia historia.

articles.title: España roza la proeza ante EEUU y luchará por llevarse el bronce
articles.standfirst: Cae en un partido en el que durante muchos minutos fue mejor que el gigante estadounidense
articles.summary: Cae en un partido en el que durante muchos minutos fue mejor que el gigante estadounidense
articles.body: España se quedó muy cerca de ganar a Estados Unidos. No es que la tuteara es que durante muchos minutos fue mejor. Pero la contundencia final del rival y el vértigo al final dejaron una derrota, 66-76, que puede resultar amarga, pero que certifica que España está muy cerca de las norteamericanas, mucho más cerca de lo que indica el marcador final. Ahora, el objetivo de las de Méndez es el bronce (16.30) este domingo. Y luego está lo de Iyana Martín que es demencial. A su edad ya se codea, por talento y posibilidades con las mejores del mundo. Hizo un partido sublime probablemente en el más importante de su vida (mañana tendrá otro). Aunque España juegue por el bronce, debe estar presente en el debate sobre la MVP del torneo. En la previa, tanto Awa Fam como Alba Torrens incidieron en que no tenían miedo a nadie (a EEUU se referían, claro) y que tenían que hacérselo sentir al rival. Y lo cumplieron desde el minuto 1. La selección salió a por el partido y lo agarró firmemente sin idea de soltarlo. El resultado fue una puesta en escena espectacular: tapón de Raquel Carrera en la primera defensa y triple de Fam en el primer ataque. Se venían cositas... La primera gran ventaja fue española, 9-1 con una canasta de María Conde. Las de Méndez atacaban de fábula y defendían muy atentas en los cambios. Con eso se lograba un 16-9 a 4:12. Pero llegó el primer momento crítico de España. Los cambios no le sentaron nada bien y sí a EEUU con las salidas de Caitlin Clark y Aliyah Boston. En cuatro minutos impusieron un parcial de 0-11 que se extendió a un 2-16 en los primeros compases del segundo acto. La selección se dejó el primer parcial, 18-21 y se vio abajo, 18-25, a 8:53 para el final. Volvieron a la pista jugadoras como Iyana Martín o Carrera y de nuevo todo se equilibró. España no le perdió la cara al partido ni siquiera con la nefasta actuación de los árbitros. La selección no lanzó su primer tiro libre hasta que faltaban 3:33 para el descanso. En ese momento EEUU llevaba lanzados 25 (con 18 aciertos). Todo demasiado desequilibrado. Una canasta mágica de puro talento de Iyana, que levantó al Uber Arena y varias buenas acciones más entregaron un 36-39 al final de los primeros 20 minutos. A pesar de los árbitros, de los tiros libres y las faltas pitadas (y técnica), España había demostrado que no tenía miedo a nadie. Y que iba a por el partido. Reanudado el juego, España seguía yendo a por la victoria. Conde, con un triple igualó el choque, 39-39, tres minutos después con otro puso por delante a su equipo, 45-44. España volvía a estar por delante en el marcador, aunque le duraría poco. Un 0-7 estadounidense en los mejores momentos de Breanna Stewart devolvió el control al vigente campeón del mundo. Iyana en pista seguía controlando el juego en ambos aros. Fabulosa la ovetense, forzando faltas y creando el desconcierto en la defensa de las estadounidenses. Ni siquiera con un continuo dos contra uno lograban limitar su producción. Llegado el final del tercer cuarto, el marcador estaba empatado, 58-58 y España imponía su juego. Habían cortado las alas a su rival no dejándole correr, la disciplina defensiva de las de Méndez era espartana, y el movimiento rápido de jugadoras y de balón en ataque no era ajustado por la defensa menos solidaria de EEUU. A España le entró cierto vértido y frenó en seco. Varias pérdidas y el hecho de que EEUU cargara más el juego interior despegaron a las estadounidenses hasta un 60-70 despúes de un 0-8 de parcial. Con viento en contra, EEUU patina, pero el viento empezaba a soplar a favor, y así se sienten más seguras. Es un equipo con fisuras y carencias, pero siguen teniendo mucho talento. En los minutos finales, varias acciones, individuales eso sí, aseguraron la victoria de EEUU. La duodécima en 12 partidos oficiales entre ambas. Iyana se fue con 17 puntos dejando una impronta de jugadora de WNBA en un futuro muy cercano. María Conde puso otros 17 y Awa Fam 9 con 7 rebotes. Y Elena Buenavida, que volvió a tener minutos, hizo un partido espectacular. En EEUU Breanna Stewart facturó 16 puntos y seis rebotes, Kahleah Copper hizo 13 y Jackie Young, actuva al final, logró 12. EEUU jugará por el oro y por su quinto entorchado seguido contra Francia este domingo (20.00), España buscará un meritoio bronce antes (16.30), frente a Alemania.

articles.summary: Team USA pulled away in the fourth quarter en route to a 77-66 win over Spain in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup semifinals on Saturday in Berlin.
articles.body:
Team USA pulled away in the fourth quarter en route to a 77-66 win over Spain in the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup semifinals on Saturday in Berlin.

USA and Spain were tied at 58 entering the fourth quarter, but the Americans sealed the win thanks to a standout stretch from Jackie Young (six fourth-quarter points) and a lockdown defensive effort.

It was a tough shooting night for Team USA, which made just 39.7 percent of its field goals, including 3-of-18 from three-point range. However, Spain also struggled to get its offense going, finishing 37.9 percent from the field and 6-of-26 from three.

The big difference was at the free-throw line. The United States made 27-of-35 attempts from the charity stripe, while Spain was 10-of-11. For comparison, Breanna Stewart was 8-of-11 from the line on her own.

The United States is seeking its fifth straight World Cup gold medal. They'll have a tough task against France, which nearly beat Team USA in the Summer Olympics' gold medal game two years ago.

France has been exceptional in this tournament, going 5-0 and outscoring its opponents by 168 points (33.6 PPG). France just beat Germany 86-64 to make Sunday's final.

Still, the Americans have been impressive and resilient in their own right and appear battle-tested after hard-fought wins over Italy and Spain.

They also excelled against China (94-61) and Czechia (105-64) in the group phase and blitzed Hungary 108-56 in the quarterfinals.

The United States and France will face off for gold on Sunday at 2 p.m. ET. It will air on TNT and truTV and stream live on HBO Max.

articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Bracket Final Preview for USA vs. France Championship
articles.summary: The United States Women's national team is headed to the 2026 FIBA World Cup Finals following a 76-66 victory over Spain, led by 16 points from Breanna Stewart.
articles.body:
The United States Women's national team is headed to the 2026 FIBA World Cup Finals following a 76-66 victory over Spain, led by 16 points from Breanna Stewart.

Team USA entered Saturday's matchup in Berlin as a 23.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , and will now take on France in the final.

Team USA led by a slim three-point margin at halftime, behind eight points from Stewart and six from Paige Bueckers. A standout fourth quarter, in which Team USA held Spain to just eight points, wrapped up the game and sent the Americans to the final.

Team USA went 3-0 in group play, earning a first-round bye and automatically qualifying for the quarterfinals. They nabbed wins over Group D opponents China, Italy and Czechia.

USA vs. France, Sunday, Sept. 11, 2 p.m. ET

Team USA is looking to add a record-breaking 12th title to its resume and win its fifth straight championship as it takes on France, which aims to put a stop to the Americans' dominant run.

France enters the matchup looking for revenge, aiming to take down a USA team it fell to in the 2024 Paris Olympics final by just one point. That U.S. team looked different, though, with A'ja Wilson and Sabrina Ionescu at the center of the action two summers ago. That hasn't been the case this time around, with Wilson choosing to skip the tournament for health reasons, while Ionescu was left off the roster.

Led by Golden State Valkyries star Gaby Williams, France has made light work of its opposition this tournament, defeating each of its five foes by at least 22 points. USA has faced much closer margins of victory, including a three-point win over Italy and Sunday's 10-point win over Spain.

The final will tip off Sunday at 2 p.m. ET on TNT, truTV and HBO Max.

articles.title: Miguel Méndez: "De entrenar sé algo, de arbitraje no tengo ni idea"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador y varias jugadoras hablaron sobre el partido ante EEUU
articles.summary: El seleccionador y varias jugadoras hablaron sobre el partido ante EEUU
articles.body: En el vestuario, se podía sentir la tristeza de España. Por la derrota, claro, no por la entrega, la competitividad, el esfuerzo o incluso el nivel, muchas veces por encima de su rival. Pero perder ante esta EEUU duele porque se pierde una oportunidad sensacional de acabar con su tiranía. España estuvo muy cerca. "Creo que ninguna persona que haya visto el partido ha tenido la más mínima duda de que nos hemos dejado la piel, de que nos hemos vaciado, de que lo hemos intentado de todas las maneras posibles, y mañana no va a ser menos. Inmensamente orgullosa del campeonato que estamos haciendo y no nos vamos a ir casa sin una medalla que plasme un mínimo de todo lo que hemos hecho para llegar hasta aquí", decía Iyana Martín en los micrófonos de Movistar+ al acabar el partido La oventense fue la mejor de España y es una de las grandes destacadas del Mundial. "Sí, realmente estamos jodidas es porque nos lo hemos creído. Sabíamos y creíamos que podíamos ganar. Hemos competido hasta el final, hemos intentado dar nuestra mejor versión; no sabría decir qué es lo que nos ha faltado en ese último cuarto, pero orgullosa del equipo", decía Raquel Carrera, que no encontraba las palabras. Orgullo es la palabra que más suena. Hemos ido a ganar y lo hemos demostra También la dijo Miguel Méndez en su intervención ante la prensa al acabar el partido: "Estoy orgulloso del partido del equipo. Hemos perdido ante un gran combinado que ha jugado mejor en los momentos clave del partido. Nos han faltado algunas cosas a final, alguna canastita fácil, pero lo hemos puesto todo. Prometimos competir y lo hemos cumplido". Del arbitraje, prefirió no hablar: "No tengo opinión del arbitraje. Sé algo de baloncesto, pero de arbitraje no tengo ni idea". Ironía en las palabras de Méndez... Sobre el partido de mañana, ante Alemania, con el bronce en juego, Méndez dijo: "Tenemos que tomarnos un tiempo de descanso, física y mentalmente, y preparar el partido lo mejor posible. Jugamos ante el anfitrión y va a ser un choque muy duro. Será un partido diferente al de la primera fase". El seleccionador acabó: "Mañana trataremos de cambiar estas caras de tristeza que tienen hoy las jugadoras por las caras de alegria que se merecen por el campeonato que han hecho".

articles.title: Nets' Michael Porter Jr. ranked 15th-best small forward this season
articles.summary: Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. was ranked as the 15th-best small forward in the NBA coming into this season, according to HoopsHype.
articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets forward Michael Porter Jr. has had a busy summer to this point as he is preparing for the upcoming NBA season while addressing whether his future will be with the Nets. Brooklyn and Porter seem like they want to continue their partnership beyond this season, but with Porter being eligible for a contract extension, it's important to note how highly he is regarded at his position.

"Porter Jr.'s current contract only runs through next season, so he'll be trying his hardest to prove he can be a top option for a team as he seeks his next big payday," Frank Urbina wrote on Porter for HoopsHype. Urbina and HoopsHype ranked the top-27 small forwards heading into this NBA campaign and Porter placed 15th on the list despite the fact that the Nets are expected to struggle once again.

"Either way, Porter Jr. has won a championship as a role player before, too; it's just that role players don't get paid as much as stars, so the Missouri product will surely be looking to prove the 2025-26 version of himself was not a fluke," Urbina continued on Porter. "Porter Jr. ranked in the Top 30 league-wide in BPM in 2025-26 thanks to his ability to shoot and hit ridiculous jumpers in his massive 6-foot-10 frame, so his production was impactful, even if his Brooklyn Nets were one of the worst teams in the league."

Porter, 28 , is coming off the best season of his season as he averaged 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds, and 3.0 assists per game while shooting 46.3% from the field and 36.3% from behind the three-point line. As Urbina pointed out, Porter and the Nets have not agreed to an extension yet, but they have until the end of this season to extend his contract for the foreseeable future.

What will be interesting to see given how Porter is viewed around the NBA is if the Nets will risk keeping him on the roster past the February trade deadline and potentially lose him for nothing next summer. Brooklyn's training camp begins at the end of this month so the organization and Porter still have some time to formally extend this partnership. If not, plenty of teams could be calling for Porter's services before the trade deadline passes.

articles.title: Ukraine’s Kate Koval transfers to Baylor following LSU exit after Tigers signed Russian player
articles.summary: Baylor signed Ukrainian center Kate Koval, the school announced Saturday, several weeks after she left LSU because Tigers coach Kim Mulkey brought in a Russian player.
articles.body: Baylor signed Ukrainian center Kate Koval, the school announced Saturday, several weeks after she left LSU because Tigers coach Kim Mulkey brought in a Russian player. Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, and the two countries have been at war since. “We are beyond excited to welcome Kate to Baylor,” Bears coach Nicki Collen said in a statement. “She has played at an elite level over the last two seasons and has shown the consistent ability to score around the rim and protect the rim. Kate, at 6-foot-5, can be a decision maker on the perimeter both as a scorer and facilitator, which will expand our offense. Her shot-blocking ability will help anchor our defense. She is an elite student with a big heart for others, and our fans will love her on and off the court.” Koval had posted on social media last week about her decision to leave LSU, saying that her father serves in the Ukrainian military and “takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression.” “For me, this war is not distant or abstract,” Koval wrote. “People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes. “The timing of this situation and the deeply personal effect it has had on me, my family, and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me. This decision has not been easy. While I understand and respect that roster decisions are a part of college basketball. I have to remain true to myself, my values, and my country.” Now Koval will be at the school that Mulkey turned into a women’s basketball powerhouse before leaving to coach the Tigers. Koval averaged 8.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 1.2 blocks last season for LSU. She started her college career at Notre Dame and averaged 5.3 points and 4.7 rebounds in the 2024-25 season.

articles.title: Former 7x All-Star showers huge praise for $49.37 million Charlotte Hornets forward ahead of NBA season opener
articles.summary: NBA News: Brandon Miller is walking into a defining year, and Tracy McGrady thinks he already has the tools to become Charlotte's next star. The seven-time All-.
articles.body: Brandon Miller is walking into a defining year, and Tracy McGrady thinks he already has the tools to become Charlotte's next star. The seven-time All-Star weighed in on Miller's trajectory as the Hornets forward prepares for his fourth NBA season, and the praise carries real weight given McGrady's own history as a franchise scorer.With LaMelo Ball now in Minnesota and Miles Bridges shipped to Phoenix, Charlotte has cleared a path for Miller to take charge. McGrady believes this is the right moment for the young wing to make his leap.Tracy McGrady showers praise on Brandon MillerSpeaking on Cousins with Vince Carter, McGrady pointed to Miller as the player who can carry the Hornets into their next chapter. The 23-year-old wing is taking on a much bigger role now that Ball has moved on, and McGrady expects it to show up in the numbers. He said Miller "should be a guy that averages 25-26 points, taking that next step."It's a bold number to hang on a young player, but McGrady clearly sees enough in Miller's game to back it up. He added that this season should reveal whether Miller becomes the franchise cornerstone Charlotte needs him to be.Last season, Miller played 65 games and averaged 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.3 assists a game, shooting 43.5 percent from the field and 38.3 percent from three. It was actually a slight dip from his second-year averages of 21 points, 4.9 rebounds and 3.6 assists on 40.3 percent shooting and 35.5 percent from deep. Numbers aside, what stands out is the trust the front office has placed in him.Hornets reshape the roster to clear Miller's pathCharlotte went through a serious shake-up this offseason. Ball was sent to the Timberwolves and Bridges was dealt to the Suns, leaving Miller and second-year wing Kon Knueppel as the clear building blocks going forward.Knueppel is coming off a strong rookie year of his own, averaging 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists while shooting 47.5 percent overall and 42.5 percent from three. The 6-foot-7 forward and Knueppel give Charlotte a modern, versatile pairing to build around, but McGrady's comments suggest Miller is the one with the higher ceiling. How Charlotte performs this season will say a lot about whether that faith was earned.Miller's rookie deal and what comes nextThe $49 million star is entering the final year of his four-year rookie contract, one that carries a 2026-27 cap hit of $15,104,626. He is now eligible for a rookie-scale extension, and Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson has confirmed the two sides have already started talking.Insiders project a new deal could land somewhere around $191 million to $200 million over five years if it gets done before the deadline. If no agreement is reached, Miller would hit restricted free agency in the summer of 2027. For now, the bigger story is what he does on the floor, and McGrady has made it clear he expects big things.The Charlotte Hornets will begin their 2026-27 NBA regular-season campaign on the road against the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday, October 21, 2026.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
